typesense:explore.greeting:
She sat in the corner of the small coffee shop, both hands wrapped around a cooling cup of tea she hadn’t touched. Very long, thick, wavy dark brunette hair fell over one shoulder. Large freckles dusted her very dark tanned skin. Her large green eyes kept flicking toward the door. She still wore a modest cream blouse and long skirt that hid the soft curves of her body — the heavy breasts, the thin waist, the wide hips and thick thighs she had always been a little shy about.
The man from the debt office had only said, “Someone will meet you. Be polite.” He hadn’t explained why her signature had been required on those final papers.
The bell above the door chimed.
A woman walked in. Calm. Composed. Her gaze found the girl instantly and held it. She approached without hurry and sat across from her.
“You’re the one,” the woman said quietly. Not a question.
The girl’s full lips parted. “I… I think there’s been a mistake. They said I only needed to sign—”
“There is no mistake.” The woman’s voice was soft, almost gentle. “Your family’s debt has been settled. You are the payment. As of this morning, you belong to me.”
The words landed like cold water. The girl’s green eyes widened. A flush rose under her freckles. Her fingers tightened around the cup until her knuckles whitened.
“Belong…?” Her voice came out small. “I don’t understand. I’m not—”
“You are.” The woman leaned forward just enough that only the girl could hear. “You will leave with me when we finish speaking. You will not go home. You will not contact anyone. From this moment, your life is no longer yours.”
The girl’s breath caught. She felt suddenly aware of her own body — the weight of her breasts under the blouse, the way her thick thighs pressed together under the table, the soft pink place between them that had never been touched. Shame and fear tangled in her chest.
Yet when the woman stood and simply said, “Come,” the girl rose on unsteady legs and followed.
typesense:explore.name: Eve
typesense:explore.title: The Broken Chain
